structured_output.analysis: The best measured grid is iso_3.15 (E514ab09c524e) with KL=0.4361 at 3.14795 avg bits. The budget is 3.1484 bits, which leaves only about 0.2M bits of slack. Upgrades therefore have to be paid for. The measured KL is higher than the predicted 0.398, which suggests interactions between layers. The layers carrying the most loss are all 3.1M-param MLP projections at int3 or int2, and moving each from int3 to int4 cuts its single-layer KL by about 0.0035–0.004 (Ef04d8aa7bded→Efea8c18d2abc, E6f4f7ea296d5→Ef8ae5e6ba828, E0564bc6ad1eb→E779bc065b72e, Efa0bb391da67→Ef428ac081334). I have KL data only for these high-loss layers, so I can't identify cheap layers to downgrade. Instead I try two things. First, act_order=true, which costs no bits. Second, freeing bits by raising rht_gptq_int3 to weight.group_size=256, which roughly halves its per-weight scale overhead, and spending them on int4 upgrades. The bit costs assume int4 is stored at 4.1484 bits per weight (int3 + 1 bit); the analysis does not state the int4 cost directly.

proposals.name: iso315_actorder
proposals.rationale: Only the options change: act_order=true is turned on for every GPTQ method. Stored bits stay the same, so the grid stays at the base's 3.14795 avg bits. The base measured KL=0.4361 [E514ab09c524e]. Most of the loss sits in MLP layers quantized with GPTQ, for example 27.up_proj at gptq_int3 with KL 0.00572 [Ef04d8aa7bded] and 14.down_proj at rht_gptq_int2 with KL 0.00633 [E4c3f9b73e065].

proposals.name: iso315_int3g256_up2
proposals.rationale: rht_gptq_int3 is set to weight.group_size=256 to save scale bits, assuming a 3.1484 bits/weight int3 cost (12.8515625 below bf16 [Eeee43f89fd9e]). The saved bits pay for upgrading two layers to rht_gptq_int4. 3.up_proj goes from 0.00642 [E6f4f7ea296d5] to 0.00245 [Ef8ae5e6ba828]. 1.up_proj goes from 0.00611 [E0564bc6ad1eb] to 0.00227 [E779bc065b72e]. The base is KL=0.4361 [E514ab09c524e].

The base is KL=0.4361 [E514ab09c524e].
